abilityDesc: The Battlerage skillset is symbolized by Kyrios, the God of Destruction. The devastating attacks of his devotees bombard their enemies mercilessly, until finally their foes kneel, bleeding, and bow before pure, destructive victory.

Dahuta, Goddess of Change, reigns over the Witchcraft skillset. She is associated with the ever-changing sea and the mysteries within; similarly, her followers shun direct damage, relying on spells that hinder or debilitate once-strong foes, mysteriously changing their constitution.

The symbol of Defense is the God of Prosperity, Shatigon, who uses his powers over the lifeforce in all living things to build impregnable fortresses of energy. His followers favor skills that increase their health or grant invincibility against hoardes of enemies.

The god most skilled in Auramancy is Haje, God of Doors and Barriers. His disciples protect allies from magic by sweeping it into otherworlds, or open doors to flood enemies with powerful magic damage. Some can even teleport through supernatural gates.

Occultism is symbolized by Nui, Goddess of Death and the Hereafter. Her gentle hands gather fallen heroes and bear them to eternal rest. Her followers then summon the powers of the fallen to inflict magic damage and terrify their foes.

The ancient plains warrior, Tahyang, pledged to protect the Firran tribes with true aim and an honest soul. He keeps this pact even in death by bestowing his powers on anyone with a pure heart. His disciples use ranged attacks to pursue foes unrelentingly and deal a vicious justice.

The ancient archmage Aranzeb symbolizes Sorcery. His followers leash powerful, unpredictable magic into versatile elemental and protection spells, just as Aranzeb once controlled his anger and sadness to confront his bloody destiny with serenity.

The assassin Melisara, known for her outrageous attempt to kill the gods, is the patron of Shadowplay. Its devotees use stealth to maneuver close to enemies before inflicting fatal wounds, or dash forward to launch lethal attacks in the span of a heartbeat.

Songcraft is a gift from Lucius, an ancient wanderer. Known for his kind heart and self-deprecating humor, he devoted his life to encouraging friends through song and music. His followers use these skills to increase allies' battle abilities and speed their movement and healing.

The Vitalism skillset is symbolized by Kyprosa, who was tasked with guarding the gate to the dream realm rather than participate in reality. Now, her disciples heal and revive fallen allies rather than participate in bloodbaths themselves, providing crucial life support in battle.

raceDetailDesc: Called the Conquerors of the Continent, Nuians possess a deeply spiritual culture that revolves around worshipping Nui, the Goddess of the Hereafter. They revere the traditions, beauty, and harmony of their fallen kingdom, and fight fearlessly to bring these traits to their new land.

Called the Conquerors of the Continent, Nuians possess a deeply spiritual culture that revolves around worshipping Nui, the Goddess of the Hereafter. They revere the traditions, beauty, and harmony of their fallen kingdom, and fight fearlessly to bring these traits to their new land.

Elves seclude themselves deep in the forest, avoiding other races as much as possible. Though envied for their beauty, their behavior is considered incomprehensible: hoping for an honorable death, they often deliberately seek out danger. They feel the ultimate honor is vengeance for their past defeats.

Harani are survivors in the truest sense of the word. Others may do anything to succeed, and meet their gods in the process, but Harani will do anything to live. Practical, cunning, and family-minded, it is no surprise the strength of their new kingdom rivals the strength of the kingdom they lost.

The restless, nomadic Firran roam the wilds, fueled by dreams of protecting nature and reclaiming their former glory. They believe every life--no matter how small--is not only valuable, but plays a critical role in the natural world, and that every Firran must strive to find their purpose and play their part.

harihara_alliance_desc: Despite their honor and propriety, this faction maintains a meticulous network of spies. Their complex laws of etiquette are designed to give them leeway to gather and swap secrets.
Relentless scheming has made the largest faction on Haranya rather notorious. However, their prominence rises from several other sources as well: innovative engineering and a superior army.
The hot climate has forged a fierce, passionate people who conduct much of their business in the coolness of the night. Their land's rare sand and unusual fruits are highly prized by outsiders.
This fertile, beautiful land has inspired its inhabitants to make art and music a central focus of their culture. It's said that for every seed that sprouts, a new song sprouts from someone's heart.
Only recently created, this faction has grown rapidly in recent years. They value history immensely and make every effort to regain memories, skills, and objects lost through the ages.
Outsiders view the Firran as a brutal, unforgiving people focused on ruthless revenge and punishing the lazy. However, the Firran are also deeply loyal, never turning their backs on those in need.

nuia_alliance_desc: Ardent worship of the Goddess Nui remains the spiritual and cultural center of Nuian life. Nowhere is that more evident than in the faith-filled lands of the Crescent Throne.
The aggressive Two Crowns faction has only recently become a major player among Nuians. They thirst to conquer, hoping to maintain the glory of the Nuian name for all eternity.
Elves have explored every inch of their new continent, but still long to return to Auroria. Their entire lives are spent seeking information and skills that will aid their homecoming.
This introverted republic has spent decades quietly developing advanced mechanical technology. They manufacture golems to use in special mining processes meant to extract rare minerals.
Royal escorts since ancient times, the Wyrdwind family still commands vast armies. They invest much of their wealth into technology to increase combat strength and mobility.
The Trieste family is known as the most signifcant patron of the arts. Many are merchants by trade, and understand that creativity is key to inspiring new--and highly marketable--inventions.

Widely respected seafarers, the Noryettes are also astute politicians, evaluating political landscapes in as great a detail as they do the tides. They are often the first to locate and recruit brilliant new minds.
outlaw_desc: Pirates delight in indiscriminate massacre and looting. Their deep love of gold can only be matched by their passion for the tension and excitement of terrorizing others.
